mainTopic: How the court's death penalties are carried out: wrong ways of doing שריפה, the method and source of הרג by the sword, and the method and source of חנק.
overview: The גמרא first finishes a parable: a תלמיד חכם starts as gold in the eyes of an עם הארץ, drops to silver, then becomes clay that cannot be fixed. Next comes the story of רב חמא בר טוביה, who burned a בת כהן with branches. רב יוסף says he erred twice: in the method of שריפה, and in judging a capital case when there is no בית המקדש. The גמרא then explains the משנה's story of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק as a court of צדוקים. It also shows that he told the חכמים about two separate burnings. A new משנה teaches that הרג is done with a sword, and רבי יהודה argues for a cleaver so as not to copy the nations. The גמרא finds a Torah source for killing a murderer by the sword and uses ״ואהבת לרעך כמוך״ to choose the kindest way. Finally, the משנה of חנק describes how strangulation is done. A ברייתא then explains why an unspecified ״מות יומת״, such as for adultery, means חנק.

steps.title: The scholar and the three goblets
steps.stepSummary: A תלמיד חכם starts out as gold in the eyes of an עם הארץ. He drops to silver once he chats with him, and becomes clay once he takes benefit from him. After that, his honor cannot be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a Torah scholar like in front of an unlearned person? At first he is like a golden goblet. Once he chats with him, he is like a silver goblet. Once he takes benefit from him, he is like a clay goblet, which can never be repaired once it breaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short parable about how a תלמיד חכם slowly loses honor in the eyes of an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each step down comes from getting closer: first casual talk, then accepting favors. Gold and silver can be melted and fixed, but broken clay cannot. So once the scholar has taken benefit, his honor in the eyes of the עם הארץ is lost for good.
steps.whatToRemember: Gold, then silver, then clay: the more a תלמיד חכם depends on an עם הארץ, the less honor he keeps, and broken clay cannot be fixed.

phrases.english: To what is a Torah scholar compared
before an ignorant person?
At first, he is like a goblet of gold.

phrases.aramaic: סִיפֵּר הֵימֶנּוּ, דּוֹמֶה לְקִיתוֹן שֶׁל כֶּסֶף.
phrases.english: Once he has chatted with him, he is like a goblet of silver.

phrases.aramaic: נֶהֱנָה מִמֶּנּוּ, דּוֹמֶה לְקִיתוֹן שֶׁל חֶרֶשׂ.
phrases.english: Once he has taken benefit from him, he is like a goblet of clay,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר, שׁוּב אֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה.
phrases.english: which, once it breaks, can never be repaired.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם דּוֹמֶה לִפְנֵי עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אגדה material that came before on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם's honor before an עם הארץ goes down step by step through chatting and taking benefit, and in the end it cannot be restored.

steps.title: רב חמא בר טוביה burns אימרתא בת טלי
steps.stepSummary: A story: אימרתא בת טלי was a בת כהן who committed adultery. רב חמא בר טוביה surrounded her with bundles of branches and burned her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אימרתא בת טלי was a priest's daughter who committed adultery. רב חמא בר טוביה surrounded her with bundles of branches and burned her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story in which a judge carried out שריפה by actually burning a woman with branches. This sets up רב יוסף's criticism in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives a בת כהן who sins this way the death penalty of שריפה. But רב חמא burned her body with a fire of branches. This is not the method the גמרא taught earlier, so the next step will judge whether he acted correctly.

phrases.english: Imrata bat Talei
was a priest's daughter who committed adultery.
(Rav) Ḥama bar Toviyya surrounded her
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word "רב" in the round brackets and some leave it out.

phrases.english: with bundles of branches and burned her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִימַּרְתָּא בַּת טָלֵי, בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁזִּינְּתָה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the parable back to the topic of the daf, which is how שריפה is carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reports an actual case: a בת כהן was put to death by burning with branches.

steps.title: רב יוסף: he made two mistakes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רב חמא בר טוביה made two mistakes. He went against רב מתנה's teaching on how to do שריפה, and he went against a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: He erred in two things. He erred regarding the teaching of רב מתנה, and he erred regarding what was taught in a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף criticizes what רב חמא did and says he made two separate mistakes. The first is named here; the second is spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first mistake is about method. רב מתנה taught that שריפה is done with a wick of molten lead, not by burning the body with branches. The second mistake goes deeper: it questions whether this court could judge a capital case at all.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
He erred in two things.
He erred regarding the teaching of Rav Mattana,
phrases.notes: This points back to רב מתנה's teaching earlier on the daf, that burning is done with a wick of lead.

phrases.english: and he erred regarding what was taught in a baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: טְעָה בְּתַרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Judges the action told in step 2 and finds it wrong.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חמא בר טוביה's execution of אימרתא בת טלי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His method went against רב מתנה's rule about the lead wick, and his judging went against a ברייתא about when capital cases may be judged.

steps.title: No death penalties without a כהן serving
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that capital cases are judged only when there is a כהן serving in the בית המקדש. Without a כהן, there is no such judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you shall come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge that will be in those days": when there is a priest, there is judgment; when there is no priest, there is no judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows רב חמא's second mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the כהנים next to the judge. From this the ברייתא learns that this kind of judging depends on כהנים serving in the בית המקדש. In רב חמא's time there was no בית המקדש, so he had no authority to give a death penalty at all.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חמא erred twice: in how he did שריפה (against רב מתנה), and in judging a capital case at all when there was no בית המקדש (against the ברייתא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reason that after the בית המקדש was destroyed, בתי דין no longer carry out the death penalty.

phrases.english: "And you shall come to the priests, the Levites,
phrases.notes: דברים 17:9

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם״ –
phrases.english: and to the judge that will be in those days" –
when there is a priest, there is judgment;
phrases.notes: He means a כהן serving in the בית המקדש, which means the בית המקדש is standing.

phrases.english: when there is no priest, there is no judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָאתָ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the ברייתא behind רב יוסף's second criticism.
steps.raayaObject: That רב חמא בר טוביה had no authority to judge a capital case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading דברים 17:9: judgment is linked to the presence of a serving כהן.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, where רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק tells of a בת כהן who sinned and was really burned. The חכמים answered that the court then was not expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר, son of רבי צדוק, said: There was an incident with a priest's daughter who committed adultery, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to a line in the משנה so it can explain it. This step sets up רב יוסף's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק saw a בת כהן burned with real fire and tried to bring a proof from it. The חכמים rejected the proof and said that court did not know the law. The גמרא now wants to know what kind of court that was.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that really happened

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said:
There was an incident with a priest's daughter who committed adultery, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." stands for the rest of the משנה: she was burned with real fire, and the חכמים said that court was not expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבַת כֹּהֵן שֶׁזִּינְּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רב חמא and goes back to a line from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's story of a בת כהן burned with real fire, which the חכמים called the act of a court that was not expert.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it was a court of צדוקים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the court in the משנה's story was a court of צדוקים. That is why they did not follow the חכמים' way of doing שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It was a court of Sadducees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why the court in the משנה's story got the law so wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים only said the court was "not expert," and it seems strange that a real בית דין would make such a basic mistake. רב יוסף says it was a court of צדוקים, who did not accept the חכמים' teachings. So that story cannot prove anything about the true halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: Sadducees: a group that rejected the teachings of the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: The story of real burning in the משנה happened in a court of צדוקים, so it proves nothing against the proper way of doing שריפה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It was a court of Sadducees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל צַדּוּקִים הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the court described in the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a proper בית דין of חכמים burned her with real fire, which would show that real burning is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court belonged to צדוקים, who did not follow the חכמים, so their act is not a source for halacha.

steps.title: A ברייתא tells the story differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the exchange in the משנה really happened that way. A ברייתא gives רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק a different story and the חכמים a different answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he really say this to them, and did they really answer him this way? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said, 'I remember when I was a little child riding on my father's shoulder. They brought a בת כהן who had committed adultery, surrounded her with bundles of branches, and burned her.' The חכמים said to him: 'You were a minor, and we do not bring proof from a minor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא tells רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's story differently from the משנה. The two versions do not seem to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים answered that the court was not expert. In the ברייתא, he was a small child, and the חכמים answered that a child's memory is no proof. The burning with bundles of branches is the same in both versions, so the difference is only in his age and in the חכמים' reply.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child who is not yet an adult
We do not bring proof (from this)

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אֲמַר לְהוּ, וְהָכִי אַהְדַּרוּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Did he say this to them, and did they answer him this way?
phrases.notes: "This" means the exchange in the משנה from step 5, where the חכמים said the court was not expert.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok said:
I remember when I was a small child
and riding on my father's shoulder,
and they brought a kohen's daughter who had committed adultery
and surrounded her with bundles of branches and burned her.
They said to him: You were a minor,
and we do not bring proof from a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אֲמַר לְהוּ, וְהָכִי אַהְדַּרוּ לֵיהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of the story quoted from the משנה in step 5 by setting it against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's account of what רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said and how the חכמים answered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has a different setting (he was a child) and a different reply (a minor's memory is no proof), so the two accounts seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: There were two separate incidents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction. Two different burnings happened, and he told the חכמים about both.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two incidents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the משנה and the ברייתא describe two different events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one event he was a child, which is the ברייתא's story. In the other he was an adult, which is the משנה's story. Each story got its own answer from the חכמים, so both sources are correct.

phrases.english: There were two incidents.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי מַעֲשִׂים הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: two separate events
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא describe one event and disagree about it.
steps.terutzMaskana: They describe two different events, each with its own reply from the חכמים.

steps.title: Which story did he tell first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what order רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק told the חכמים his two stories.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one did he tell them first?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that there are two stories, the גמרא asks which one he told first. This sets up the next two steps, which work out the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matters. A sensible person would not follow a stronger proof that was rejected with a weaker one. So the order has to make sense with how the חכמים answered.

phrases.english: Which did he tell them first?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי אֲמַר לְהוּ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 8 that there were two stories.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The order in which the two stories were told to the חכמים.

steps.title: The adult story could not have come first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that he first told the story from when he was an adult. If they ignored that one, why would he expect them to accept a childhood memory?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he told them the first one first, then he told them what he saw as an adult and they paid no attention to him. Would he then tell them what he saw as a child and expect them to pay attention to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible order and rejects it because it does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something seen as an adult is a stronger proof than a child's memory. If the חכמים already brushed off the stronger proof, it would be strange to follow up with a weaker one. So the adult story could not have been first.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (it opens a possibility that will be rejected)

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא הָא קַמַּיְיתָא אֲמַר לְהוּ בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: If you say he told them this first one first,
phrases.notes: "This first one" is the משנה's story, the one that happened when he was an adult.

phrases.english: he told what he saw when he was an adult,
and they paid no attention to him.
Would he then tell them what he saw when he was a child,
and expect them to pay attention to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא הָא קַמַּיְיתָא אֲמַר לְהוּ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 9's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the order in which the adult story came first.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No one would follow a rejected strong proof with a weaker one.

steps.title: First the childhood story, then the adult story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that he first told the childhood story, and they said he was a minor. Then he told the adult story, and they said that court was not expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he told them that one first, and they said to him: 'You were a minor.' Then he told them what he saw as an adult, and they said to him: 'That is because the court of that time was not expert.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the order that makes sense: the weaker story first, then the stronger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the childhood story was rejected because he was a minor, he moved to a stronger proof from when he was an adult. The חכמים then answered in a new way: the event really happened, but that court did not know the correct practice. This fits both the ברייתא and the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: There were two stories. The childhood one was rejected because he was a minor. The adult one was rejected because that court was not expert. So the practice of actually burning the body is not the accepted halacha.

phrases.english: Rather, he told them that one first,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא's story, from when he was a child.

phrases.english: and they said to him: You were a minor,
and then he told them what he saw when he was an adult,
and they said to him: It is because there was not

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה בָּקִי.
phrases.english: an expert court at that time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָא אֲמַר לְהוּ בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 rejects one order, this step gives the correct order.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First the childhood story (rejected because he was a minor), then the adult story (rejected because that court was not expert).

steps.title: משנה: הרג is done with a sword
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. The תנא קמא says that for those killed by הרג, the court cuts off the head with a sword, the way the government does.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The מצוה of those who are killed: they would cut off his head with a sword, the way the government does.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: how the death penalty of הרג is carried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having finished discussing שריפה, the משנה now describes הרג. The first opinion says to use a sword, like a king's executioner does.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (it marks the start of a new משנה)
Those put to death by הרג (the sword)
Cut off (so the head falls away)

phrases.english: MISHNA: The מצוה of those who are killed:
phrases.notes: This means the proper way to carry out the death penalty of הרג.

phrases.english: they would cut off his head with a sword,
the way the government does.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִצְוַת הַנֶּהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new method of execution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הרג is carried out by cutting off the head with a sword.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a sword is degrading, so use a cleaver on a block
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה objects that using a sword degrades the person. Instead, the head is placed on a block and cut off with a cleaver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: That is degrading to him. Rather, they place his head on the block and chop it off with a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and gives a different method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's concern is the person's dignity. He thinks the sword method is degrading, so he wants the head on a block and cut with a cleaver.

keyTerms.meaning: A block, like a chopping block
A cleaver, a butcher's chopping knife

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נִיוּוּל הוּא לוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It is degrading to him,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַנִּיחִין אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ עַל הַסַּדָּן
phrases.english: rather, they place his head on the block
and chop it off with a cleaver.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נִיוּוּל הוּא לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion on the method in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The head is put on a block and cut off with a cleaver, to avoid degrading the person.

steps.title: The חכמים: no death is more degrading than that
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that his method is actually the most degrading way to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There is no death more degrading than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה using his own reason, dignity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה wanted to avoid degradation. The חכמים say a block and cleaver, the way a butcher cuts, is even more degrading than a sword. So his own concern supports the sword.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees we should avoid degrading the person. They argue about which method is less degrading, and the חכמים say the sword is better.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מִיתָה מְנוֶּוּלֶת מִזּוֹ.
phrases.english: They said to him: There is no death more degrading than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מִיתָה מְנוֶּוּלֶת מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's method from step 13 using his own reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His method is even more degrading than the sword, so it fails his own goal of avoiding degradation.

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains why he still uses the cleaver
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה agreeing that his method is degrading, but saying he has no choice because the Torah forbids copying the nations' practices.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said to the חכמים, 'I also know it is a degrading death. But what can I do? The Torah says: And in their statutes you shall not walk.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה answers the חכמים' complaint from the משנה. He agrees with them, but says the Torah forces his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not argue about which death is more degrading. His real point is that the sword is how the government executes people, so using it would copy the nations' practice. The cleaver is the lesser of two problems.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not follow the practices of the nations (ויקרא 18:3)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying the cleaver is more respectful. He admits it is degrading. He objects to the sword only because it copies non-Jewish practice.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a ברייתא
Rabbi Yehuda said to the Sages

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁמִּיתָה מְנוּוֶּלֶת הִיא
phrases.english: I too know that it is a degrading death
but what shall I do
for the Torah said
"And in their statutes you shall not walk."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:3

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא, אמר להן רבי יהודה לחכמים: אף אני יודע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' objection in step 14 by giving רבי יהודה's real reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the factual point and moves the argument to a different principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed רבי יהודה thought the cleaver was more respectful.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees it is degrading, but avoids the sword because the Torah forbids following the nations' practices.

steps.title: The Sages: the sword comes from the Torah, not from the nations
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are not worried about copying the nations, because death by the sword is written in the Torah itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? Since the sword is written in the Torah, we are not learning it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the חכמים deal with רבי יהודה's argument, and answers that the sword is already in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is against taking on a practice because the nations do it. If the Torah itself commands the practice, we are doing it because of the Torah. It does not matter that the nations happen to do the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not learning it from them

phrases.english: And the Sages?
phrases.notes: Short for: how do the Sages answer רבי יהודה's argument?

phrases.english: since the sword is written in the Torah
we are not learning it from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבנן, כיון דכתיב סייף באורייתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's reasoning from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using ״וּבְחֻקֹּתֵיהֶם לֹא תֵלֵכוּ״ against the sword.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The prohibition does not apply to a practice the Torah itself commands.

steps.title: Proof from burning items when a king dies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the חכמים' principle with a ברייתא that allows burning items when a king dies, even though the nations seem to have a similar custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you do not say this, then look at the ברייתא: 'We burn items over kings, and it is not one of the ways of the אמורי.' How could we burn? It is written: And in their statutes you shall not walk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It shows that without the חכמים' principle, a permitted custom would be impossible to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא permits burning items at a king's death and says it is not a forbidden non-Jewish custom. But if every practice the nations share were forbidden, this burning should also break ״וּבְחֻקֹּתֵיהֶם לֹא תֵלֵכוּ״. The question shows that some principle must permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning items over the death of kings, as a sign of honor and mourning
The ways of the Emori: forbidden non-Jewish customs
For if you do not say so (introduces a proof)

phrases.english: For if you do not say so
then that which is taught in a ברייתא
one burns items over kings
phrases.notes: This means burning a dead king's belongings as a sign of mourning and honor.

phrases.english: and it is not of the ways of the Emori
how can we burn?
But it is written: "And in their statutes you shall not walk"!

steps.triggerLanguage: דאי לא תימא הכי, הא דתניא: שורפין על המלכים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for the principle stated in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that a practice written in the Torah is not forbidden as copying the nations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא permitting burning items over kings.

steps.title: Burning for kings is in the פסוקים, so the sword is also allowed
steps.stepSummary: Burning for kings is allowed because a פסוק mentions it, and the sword is allowed for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since burning is written in the Torah, as it says: 'And with the burnings of your fathers...', we are not learning it from them. Here too, since the sword is written in the Torah, we are not learning it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It gives the reason burning is allowed and applies the same reason to the sword.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning for kings is mentioned in ירמיהו, so it is a Jewish practice and not taken from the nations. The sword is written in the Torah too, so the חכמים do not need to worry about ״וּבְחֻקֹּתֵיהֶם לֹא תֵלֵכוּ״. This fully explains the חכמים' position against רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And with the burnings of your fathers (ירמיהו 34:5)
And here too (applies the proof to our case)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, ״וּבְחֻקֹּתֵיהֶם לֹא תֵלֵכוּ״ does not forbid a practice that our own holy texts command or describe, even if the nations do it too.

phrases.english: Rather, since burning is written in the Torah
as it is written: "And with the burnings of your fathers, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 34:5. "Torah" here is used broadly for the פסוקים of תנ״ך.

phrases.english: we are not learning it from them.
And here too
since the sword is written in the Torah
we are not learning it from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא, כיון דכתיב שריפה באורייתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 17 and applies the answer back to the sword.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sword is permitted because it comes from the Torah, so ״וּבְחֻקֹּתֵיהֶם לֹא תֵלֵכוּ״ does not apply.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a murderer is killed by the sword?
steps.stepSummary: A later משנה lists the רוצח and the אנשי עיר הנדחת among those killed by the sword. The עיר הנדחת has a פסוק, but what is the source for the רוצח?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה in another chapter says: 'These are the ones killed by the sword: the רוצח and the people of an עיר הנדחת.' The עיר הנדחת makes sense, since 'by the edge of the sword' is written about them. But the רוצח, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants the Torah source for killing a רוצח by the sword.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים just said the sword is 'written in the Torah,' so the גמרא checks where. For the עיר הנדחת there is a clear פסוק, ״לְפִי חָרֶב״. For a רוצח, no פסוק has been shown yet, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: In another chapter of our מסכתא
A city that was led into עבודה זרה
By the edge of the sword (דברים 13:16)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a משנה in another chapter
These are the ones who are killed by the sword
the murderer, and the people of an idolatrous city.
Granted, the idolatrous city
it is written about them: "by the edge of the sword"
phrases.notes: דברים 13:16

phrases.english: But a murderer, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: והא דתנן באידך פירקין: אלו הן הנהרגין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the sword is written in the Torah, the גמרא looks for the specific source for a רוצח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for executing a רוצח by the sword.

steps.title: The word 'avenged' points to the sword
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the shared word 'נקם' that a man who kills his slave is killed by the sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the Torah says the killer of a slave 'shall surely be avenged,' but we don't know what kind of vengeance that means. Another פסוק says 'I will bring upon you a sword avenging the vengeance of the covenant.' So this vengeance must mean the sword.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 19 about a source for the רוצח. It brings a ברייתא that connects the word 'vengeance' in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about killing a slave says 'נקם ינקם' but does not say how. A different פסוק uses the same word 'נקם' together with 'sword.' So the ברייתא concludes that this vengeance is death by the sword.

keyTerms.meaning: Vengeance; here, the punishment for killing a slave
You must therefore say; introduces the conclusion
Death by the sword (cutting off the head)

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'He shall surely be avenged'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:20

phrases.aramaic: נְקִימָה זוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה הִיא.
phrases.english: This vengeance, I do not know what it is.
When it says:
'And I will bring upon you a sword avenging the vengeance of the covenant,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:25

phrases.english: you must say: this vengeance is the sword.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 about the source for killing a רוצח by the sword.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word 'נקם' links the slave-killer to the 'avenging sword,' so he is killed by סייף.

steps.title: Why not stab him with the sword?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the sword should be used to stab him, not to cut off his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the sword should be used by stabbing him with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the punishment is the sword, but now challenges how it is used. It sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only proved that a sword is used. It did not prove whether the head is cut off or whether the person is stabbed with the point.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead; introduces another possibility

phrases.english: But say that he should stab him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: דְּבָרֵיז לֵיהּ מִיבְרָז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the sword from step 20 is used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that סייף means cutting off the head
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sword can also kill by stabbing, so the proof does not tell us the method.

steps.title: The פסוק says the edge of the sword
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'לפי חרב,' the edge of the sword, so it means cutting, not stabbing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'with the edge of the sword'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah says 'the edge of the sword,' so the killing is done with the sharp edge, not the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stabbing uses the point of the sword, but cutting uses the edge. Since the פסוק mentions the edge, the method must be cutting off the head.

keyTerms.meaning: With the edge of the sword

phrases.english: 'With the edge of the sword' is written!
phrases.notes: דברים 13:16, about the עיר הנדחת. Literally 'by the mouth of the sword,' meaning its sharp edge.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לְפִי חָרֶב״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק that specifies the edge of the sword
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sword might be used to stab.
steps.terutzMaskana: The edge of the sword is used, so it is cutting, not stabbing.

steps.title: Why not cut him in half?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the edge of the sword could also cut his body in half down the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he should cut him in half?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further: even using the edge, maybe the body should be split down the middle. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'edge of the sword' rule out stabbing, but not every kind of cutting. Splitting the body in half also uses the edge.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting the body in half, down the middle

phrases.english: But say that he should cut him in half?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא דְּעָבֵיד לֵיהּ גִּיסְטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method again, even after step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the edge means cutting off the head
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting the body in half also uses the edge, so 'edge of the sword' does not decide between them.

steps.title: Love your neighbor: choose a kind death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says that 'love your neighbor as yourself' requires choosing a kind death for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the פסוק says 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Choose a good death for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that cutting him in half is not allowed, because the Torah tells us to love even this person and give him a kind death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even someone sentenced to death is still a 'neighbor.' So among the possible ways to use the sword, the court must pick the gentlest one, which is cutting off the head.

keyTerms.meaning: Choose for him a good (kind) death

steps.whatToRemember: סייף means cutting off the head: the word 'נקם' teaches the sword, 'לפי חרב' teaches the edge, and 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך' rules out a cruel way of cutting.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The verse says: 'And you shall love your neighbor as yourself,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: choose for him a good death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a general Torah principle that limits the method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The body might be cut in half.
steps.terutzMaskana: A kind death must be chosen, so the head is cut off.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'בְּרוֹר לוֹ מִיתָה יָפָה' shapes how all the court's death penalties are carried out.

steps.title: What about someone who kills a free person?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only spoke about killing a slave; the גמרא asks for a source for killing a free person.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for someone who killed a slave. Where do we learn it for a free person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the source in step 20 only covers killing a slave. It asks for a source for killing a free person, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'נקם ינקם' is written about a man who kills his slave. That does not automatically show that the killer of a free person gets the same death, so a further source is needed.

phrases.english: We have found one who killed a slave;
a free person, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן דִּקְטַל עַבְדָּא, בַּר חוֹרִין מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the source from step 20 is limited to a slave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that one who kills a free person is also killed by the sword.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the slave case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a קל וחומר proves it: if killing a slave is punished by the sword, killing a free person can't get the lighter חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it a קל וחומר? If someone who killed a slave is killed by the sword, should someone who killed a free person only be strangled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 25 with simple logic. Murdering a free person is surely no less serious than murdering a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already taught that killing a slave is punished with סייף. A free person is more important than a slave, so the murderer of a free person should not get an easier death than סייף. This assumes that סייף is a harsher death than חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a lighter case to a stricter case: if it is true there, it is surely true here
Strangulation, one of the four court executions
The sword; execution by cutting off the head

phrases.english: But is it not a kal vachomer?
One who killed a slave is executed by the sword,
and one who killed a free person only by strangling?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in step 25 for a source for killing a free person with the sword.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the slave case: a free person's murderer can't get a lighter death than a slave's murderer.

steps.title: The קל וחומר only works if strangling is the lighter death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the קל וחומר: it works only for the view that חנק is lighter than סייף. For the view that חנק is harsher, the proof falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says strangling is lighter. But according to the one who says strangling is harsher, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the קל וחומר from step 26. It points out that there is a disagreement about which death is harsher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר needs a clear 'lighter' and 'stricter.' If חנק is harsher than סייף, then giving a free person's murderer חנק would actually be stricter, which fits the קל וחומר even better. So the logic no longer proves that he gets סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
What can be said? (the answer doesn't work for this view)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the free person's murderer really gets חנק. It is only showing that the קל וחומר can't prove סייף for everyone, so a different source is needed.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says strangling is lighter,
but according to the one who says strangling is harsher,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר given in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר works only for the view that חנק is lighter; it fails for the view that חנק is harsher.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depends on which execution is harsher, and that is a matter of disagreement.

steps.title: All murderers are compared to the עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new source: a ברייתא compares all murderers to the עגלה ערופה, which is killed with a blade at the neck, so murderers get סייף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from what a ברייתא teaches: 'And you shall remove the innocent blood from among you.' All who spill blood are compared to the עגלה ערופה. Just as there it is with a sword and at the neck, so too here it is with a sword and at the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a source from a פסוק that works for everyone. The פסוק about the עגלה ערופה links it to all murderers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the עגלה ערופה speaks of removing 'innocent blood,' which connects it to every case of murder. Because of this link (a היקש), murderers are killed the same way as the עגלה ערופה: with a blade at the neck. This proof does not depend on whether חנק or סייף is harsher.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared (a היקש, linking two things from a פסוק)
The calf whose neck is broken, brought when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
Just as there, so too here (the pattern of a comparison)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real source for why a murderer, even of a free person, is executed by סייף.

phrases.english: He learns it from what was taught in a baraita:
"And you shall remove the innocent blood from among you":
phrases.notes: דברים 21:9

phrases.english: all spillers of blood are compared
to the eglah arufah.
Just as there, it is with a sword and at the neck,
so too here, it is with a sword and at the neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected קל וחומר with a source from a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed a קל וחומר, which fails for the view that חנק is harsher.
steps.terutzMaskana: Murderers are compared to the עגלה ערופה, so they are killed by a blade at the neck.

steps.title: Should the murderer be killed exactly like the עגלה ערופה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if murderers are compared to the עגלה ערופה, maybe they should be killed exactly the same way, with a cleaver from the back of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there it is with a cleaver and from the back of the neck, so too here it should be with a cleaver and from the back of the neck?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the comparison from step 28 and pushes it further. If the עגלה ערופה is the model, why not copy every detail?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה is killed with a heavy chopping blade from the back of the neck. If the comparison is complete, the murderer should be killed the same way. That would be a harsher, uglier death than the regular סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaver, a heavy chopping blade
From the back of the neck

phrases.english: If so, just as there
it is with a cleaver and from the back of the neck,
so too here, with a cleaver and from the back of the neck?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי, מָה לְהַלָּן בְּקוֹפִיץ וּמִמּוּל עוֹרֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison in step 28 goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of murderers to the עגלה ערופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, every detail of the עגלה ערופה (cleaver, back of the neck) should apply to the murderer too.

steps.title: Love your neighbor: choose a kind death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה answers from 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך': we must choose a kind death for him, so the harsh details of the עגלה ערופה are not copied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The פסוק says, 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Choose for him a kind death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 29. The basic method (a blade at the neck) comes from the עגלה ערופה, but the details must be the kindest way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison teaches the type of death: סייף at the neck. But 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך' tells us that even a condemned man should get the least painful version. So we do not use a cleaver from the back of the neck.

keyTerms.meaning: Choose for him a kind (good) death

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same teaching of רב נחמן from step 24. There it ruled out cutting the body in half; here it rules out the cleaver from the back of the neck. Same rule, new use.
steps.whatToRemember: A murderer is executed by סייף at the neck, learned from the עגלה ערופה. But the way it is done must be the kindest possible, because of 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabbah bar Avuh:
The verse says, "Love your neighbor as yourself":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: choose for him a kind death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29 using the same teaching as step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison with a second פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every detail of the עגלה ערופה, including the cleaver from the back of the neck, should apply to the murderer.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the basic method (blade at the neck) is copied; the details must be the kindest death, because of 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך.'

steps.title: How strangulation is carried out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the procedure for executing someone sentenced to חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The way to carry out strangulation: they sink the person in dung up to his knees. A rough cloth is placed inside a soft cloth and wrapped around his neck. One person pulls one end toward himself and another pulls the other end toward himself, until he dies.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains step by step how the court carries out the death penalty of חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail has a job. The dung holds the person still. The rough cloth inside the soft one lets the cloth tighten without tearing the skin. Two people pulling from opposite sides tighten it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the text the גמרא will discuss
Those sentenced to death by strangulation

phrases.english: MISHNA: The procedure for those who are strangled:
They would sink him
in dung up to his knees,
and one places a rough cloth
inside the soft one,
and wraps it around his neck.
This one pulls toward himself
and that one pulls toward himself,
until his soul departs.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִצְוַת הַנֶּחְנָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of סייף ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנק is done by sinking the person in dung to his knees and having two people pull a cloth wrapped around his neck from opposite sides.

steps.title: Who is excluded from the adultery death penalty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק about adultery word by word and lists three cases that are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'A man' leaves out a minor. 'Who sins with a man's wife' leaves out the wife of a minor. 'His neighbor's wife' leaves out the wife of others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק of adultery, which is one of the sins punished by חנק. It starts by listing who is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק narrows the law. A minor who sins is not punished. Sinning with a minor's wife is not this sin, because a minor's marriage does not count. The wife of 'others' (a non-Jew) is not 'his neighbor's wife'.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, someone not yet of age

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
'A man' excludes a minor,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:10

phrases.english: 'who commits adultery with a man's wife'
excludes the wife of a minor,
'his neighbor's wife'
excludes the wife of others.
phrases.notes: 'Others' here means a non-Jew, who is not called 'his neighbor'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה by bringing a ברייתא about a sin punished by חנק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The adultery death penalty does not apply to a minor, to the wife of a minor, or to the wife of a non-Jew.

steps.title: Which death does 'מות יומת' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'מות יומת' means חנק, then asks how we know it isn't one of the other death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He shall be put to death' means by strangulation. Do you say by strangulation, or maybe it is one of the other death penalties written in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states that adultery is punished by חנק and then asks why it couldn't be another death penalty. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'מות יומת' and doesn't say which death. The תורה has four kinds of death penalty, so the question is how we choose חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall surely be put to death
Do you say... or is it perhaps...; a way of opening a question
The death penalties mentioned in the תורה

phrases.english: 'Shall be put to death' means by strangulation.
Do you say by strangulation,
or is it rather by one
of all the deaths stated in the תורה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּחֶנֶק, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאַחַת מִכׇּל מִיתוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק and moves from who is punished to how they are punished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that an unspecified 'מות יומת' means חנק and not another death?

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: an unclear death penalty is read the lenient way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה answers that when the תורה gives a death penalty without details, we must choose the lighter option, which is חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say: whenever the תורה mentions death without details, you may not stretch it to be strict. You may only read it to be lenient. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question from the last step. רבי יאשיה gives a general rule for reading an unclear death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק doesn't say which death, we have no right to choose a harsher one. So we pick the lightest, and that is חנק.

phrases.english: You must say:
Anywhere that death is stated
in the תורה without details,
you are not permitted to draw it
toward strictness,
but only toward leniency.
These are the words of רבי יאשיה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר מִיתָה בְּתוֹרָה סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An unspecified death penalty must be read leniently, so it is חנק, the lightest death.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: unspecified death is always חנק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן agrees the answer is חנק but rejects the reason. He holds there is a set rule that any unspecified death in the תורה is חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: not because it is the light one. Rather, every death the תורה mentions without details is only strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different reason for the same result. רבי יונתן doesn't rely on 'choose the lenient one'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יאשיה, חנק wins because it is the lightest. For רבי יונתן, it doesn't matter whether חנק is light or harsh. The rule is that an unspecified death always means חנק, and the other deaths have to be written out clearly.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that a death penalty without details means חנק. They argue only about why: רבי יאשיה says it is because we choose the lightest death, and רבי יונתן says it is simply the set rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יונתן disagrees about the halacha. He gives the same answer, חנק, and only rejects the reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says:
It is not because it is the light one;
rather, every death stated
in the תורה without details
is nothing other than strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the reasoning of רבי יאשיה in step 34 but keeps his conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any death penalty the תורה states without details is חנק. This is a fixed rule, not based on חנק being the lightest.

steps.title: רבי compares court death to death from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that just as מיתה בידי שמים leaves no mark on the body, an unspecified death by the court must also leave no mark. That means חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: The תורה speaks of death by Heaven, and it also speaks of death by people, meaning the court. Death by Heaven leaves no mark on the body. So the court's death must also be one that leaves no mark.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a third way to explain why an unspecified death in the תורה means חנק. He compares the court's death to death 'from Heaven'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה said we choose the lightest death, and רבי יונתן said it is a set rule. רבי instead learns it from a comparison. Both kinds of death are called 'מיתה' in the תורה, so they must share a feature: no outer mark on the body, and חנק fits that description.

keyTerms.meaning: Death at the hand of Heaven, a punishment ה׳ carries out, not the court
Death at the hands of people, a death penalty carried out by בית דין
A mark or visible sign on the body
'Just as … so too …', the standard way of making a comparison

phrases.english: Rebbi says:
Death at the hand of Heaven is stated [in the Torah],
and death at the hands of a person is stated [in the Torah].
Just as the death stated at the hand of Heaven
is a death that leaves no mark,
so too the death stated at the hands of a person
is a death that leaves no mark.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר מִיתָה בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion, alongside רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן, explaining why an unspecified death is חנק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified court death leaves no mark on the body, just like death from Heaven, so it is חנק.

steps.title: Why not say burning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: שריפה also leaves no outer mark, so maybe that is the death meant here.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it means burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רבי's comparison. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's rule only says 'a death with no mark'. שריפה (done by pouring something burning inside the body) also leaves no outer mark. So the comparison alone does not prove the answer is חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say …', introducing another possibility that challenges what was just said
Execution by burning, one of the four court death penalties

phrases.english: But say [it is] burning?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא שְׂרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's comparison as not narrow enough to point only to חנק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's proof that 'a death with no mark' must be חנק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שריפה also leaves no outer mark, so the comparison does not rule it out.

steps.title: The תורה singles out a בת כהן for burning
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה says specifically that a בת כהן who sins is burned, we see that an ordinary adulteress is not burned. That leaves חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the תורה says that a כהן's daughter is punished by burning, it follows that this ordinary woman is not someone who gets burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points to a separate פסוק that gives שריפה only to a בת כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every adulteress were already burned, the תורה would not need to say that a בת כהן is burned. Singling her out shows that a regular adulteress gets a different death. So the 'no mark' death for her must be חנק, and רבי's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', a way of referring to ה׳ as the One who wrote the תורה
'By implication …', drawing a conclusion from what a פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: The adulterer's 'מות יומת' is חנק. רבי learns it from comparing it to מיתה בידי שמים, which leaves no mark. שריפה is ruled out because the תורה gives it only to a בת כהן.

phrases.english: From [the fact] that the Merciful One said a priest's daughter is [executed] by burning,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:9

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּהָא לָאו בַּת שְׂרֵיפָה הִיא.
phrases.english: it is implied that this [woman] is not liable to burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא בַּת כֹּהֵן בִּשְׂרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 37 and saves רבי's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference from a separate פסוק that limits שריפה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since שריפה also leaves no mark, the unspecified death might be שריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the תורה gives שריפה specifically to a בת כהן, an ordinary adulteress is not burned, so her death is חנק.
